raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
### What does this PR do?

Makes DeepSeek-V4-Flash GRPO run end to end on AMD MI355X with an FP8 rollout, and gives it one recipe with three training modes. Follow-up to #7050 (ROCm enablement) and #7455 / #7470 (Megatron-Bridge path). Two commits:

1. **`[docker]` image.** `docker/rocm/Dockerfile.rocm.deepseek-v4` builds the versions the runs were validated with: Transformer Engine 2.18 (ROCm build: Triton grouped GEMM path that avoids a bf16 grouped-GEMM backward hang on gfx950, float-scale blockwise FP8 GEMM), a libhsa-runtime that returns memory under `expandable_segments` on ROCm 7.2.x, Megatron-LM `fd1121b8f` plus the `deepseek-v4-rocm-support` commits (config-driven FP8 fake quantization, FP8-training alignment options, and the `index_select` gather of the unfused CSA sparse attention that upstream introduced with the reworked SBHD path in NVIDIA/Megatron-LM#6400, which this older base predates), Megatron-Bridge 0.5.0 plus a fix that keeps the FP8 weight export on the checkpoint's power-of-two scale grid, and four vLLM 0.26.0 patches applied at build time (NaN guard on the FP8 indexer logits; CuMem wake cache release, vllm#49857; indexer K-cache block-flat layout on gfx950/gfx942, vllm#50455; SwiGLU clamp on the FP8 Triton fused MoE path).
2. **`[recipe]` one script, three modes.** `examples/grpo_trainer/run_deepseek_v4_flash_megatron_rocm.sh`, `TRAIN_MODE=qat|fp8|bf16`. `qat` is BF16 training with Megatron's FP8 fake quantization (weights on 128x128 power-of-two scales, inputs on 1x128 float scales, straight-through estimator) and an FP8 W8A8 vLLM rollout; `fp8` is Transformer Engine blockwise FP8 training with float activation scales; `bf16` is BF16 training with a BF16 rollout. All modes round the KV latent and the indexer q/k the way the rollout's FP8 KV cache and FP8 indexer do. Everything is a transformer-config override; the only environment variables are the two Transformer Engine kernel selectors.

Why the alignment matters: on ROCm, vLLM quantizes FP8 activations with float scales (amax / 448) while Transformer Engine's blockwise recipe uses powers of two, so the same training code that aligns on NVIDIA (DeepGEMM) does not align here. With the rollout's rounding reproduced in training, `training/rollout_probs_diff_mean` at step 1 drops to the BF16-forward level and the train/rollout KL stays flat over 300 steps.

The Megatron-LM and Megatron-Bridge changes live in the author's forks while they are proposed upstream; the Transformer Engine wheel and the libhsa-runtime are published as release assets because no official ROCm package carries those fixes yet.

### Checklist Before Starting

- [x] Search for similar PRs. https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+deepseek-v4+rocm
- [x] Format the PR title as `[{modules}] {type}: {description}`

### Test

DeepSeek-V4-Flash (FP8 checkpoint), 4 nodes x 8 MI355X, ROCm 7.2.3, GRPO/GSPO on DAPO-Math, validated on AIME-2024 every 10 steps:

| Mode | step-1 `rollout_probs_diff_mean` | step-1 `rollout_corr/kl` | 300 steps | AIME-2024 acc |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| qat | 0.0096 | 0.0021 | KL 0.0022 -> 0.0029, no NaN/hang | 0.60 -> 0.76 |
| fp8 | 0.0097 | 0.0021 | KL 0.0022 -> 0.0039 | 0.60 -> 0.76 |
| bf16 | 0.0060 | 0.0008 | KL 0.0008 -> 0.0011 | 0.59 -> 0.79 peak |

On the image built from this branch, a 7-layer cut of the model (single node) gives diff / KL of 0.0129 / 0.0068 in `qat` and 0.0130 / 0.0069 in `fp8` over 3 steps, matching the earlier runs. Per step on 32 GPUs: ~490 s (`qat`), ~420 s (`fp8`), ~330 s (`bf16`), of which ~85 s is the weight sync.

### API and Usage Example

```bash
DOCKER_BUILDKIT=1 docker build -f docker/rocm/Dockerfile.rocm.deepseek-v4 -t rocm-verl-dsv4 .
# Ray on every node (commands in the script header), then on the head node:
WK=<wandb key> TRAIN_MODE=qat bash examples/grpo_trainer/run_deepseek_v4_flash_megatron_rocm.sh
TRAIN_MODE=fp8 TOTAL_TRAINING_STEPS=5 bash examples/grpo_trainer/run_deepseek_v4_flash_megatron_rocm.sh trainer.val_before_train=False
```

### Design & Code Changes

- `docker/rocm/Dockerfile.rocm.deepseek-v4`: version pins and build-time patches as described; `docker/rocm/patches/vllm-*.patch` carry the upstream reference in their headers.
- `examples/grpo_trainer/run_deepseek_v4_flash_megatron_rocm.sh`: the recipe; the header documents the modes, the Ray commands and the reference values. The mode only changes a set of `override_transformer_config` keys (`fp8_fake_quant`, `fp8_fake_quant_kv_cache`, `fp8_fake_quant_indexer_qk`, and for `fp8`: `fp8=e4m3 fp8_recipe=blockwise fp8_blockwise_act_pow2_scale=False`), applied to both the actor and the reference policy.

### Checklist Before Submitting

- [x] Read the [Contribute Guide](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
- [x] Apply [pre-commit checks](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#code-linting-and-formatting)
- [ ] Add / Update the documentation: the recipe header is the documentation; happy to add a docs page if preferred.
- [ ] Add unit or end-to-end test(s): needs 32 MI355X and the DeepSeek-V4 checkpoint; validated by the runs above.
- [ ] Once your PR is ready for CI, send a message in the `ci-request` channel.

nodes.body: This patch also apply on CUDA platform?
nodes.diffHunk:
@@ -161,6 +245,7 @@ def apply_patch():
     # creation (hf_to_mcore_config_dpskv3) and after it in
     # megatron_utils.make_megatron_module, so the shim also back-fills importers.
     apply_fast_hadamard_transform_shim()
+    apply_patch_csa_unfused_sparse_attn()

nodes.body:
Answering my own question after checking: **yes, this patch also applies on CUDA**, and I'd prefer not to land it in its current form.

- `apply_patch()` runs for every `MLATransformerConfig` model (`hf_to_mcore_config_dpskv3` and `make_megatron_module`), regardless of platform. The new function only checks whether `csa` can be imported, and any recent mcore has that module.
- CUDA reaches the unfused path too. In `fd1121b8f`, `apply_dsa_kernel_fusion` defaults to `False`. In upstream `main`, `use_fused_dsa_kernels(config)` falls back to unfused when the backend is unfused or when FlashMLA / cuDNN CuTe-DSL is missing. All call sites in `csa.py` resolve the name from the module globals, so the replacement is used everywhere.

More importantly, **upstream has already fixed this**. NVIDIA/Megatron-LM#6400 (`a2003d48f`, merged 2026-08-27) changed `unfused_compressed_sparse_attn` to `kv_flat.index_select(0, ...)` with the same rationale. Your fork's base `fd1121b8f` (2026-07-10) predates it. With an mcore that already has the fix, this patch:
- overwrites the upstream implementation with a frozen copy and drops upstream's `attn_sink` shape validation;
- will break (`TypeError`) or silently diverge if upstream later changes the signature or the index semantics (e.g. THD);
- is applied silently, with no log line, so it would be hard to spot during debugging.

Suggestions:
1. Preferred: cherry-pick #6400 into the `deepseek-v4-rocm-support` fork (or rebase onto a newer mcore), point the Dockerfile at it, and drop this verl patch.
2. If it has to stay for now, gate it on the old implementation rather than on the platform, e.g. only patch when `"torch.gather" in inspect.getsource(csa.unfused_compressed_sparse_attn)`, and log when the patch is applied. CUDA users on an old mcore with fusion off would hit the same OOM, so an `is_rocm` check alone isn't the right gate.

The Dockerfile, vLLM patches and recipe are ROCm-only and don't affect CUDA.

@@ -3,47 +3,72 @@ FROM vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:v0.26.0 AS verl_base
 
 RUN --mount=type=cache,target=/root/.cache/pip \
     pip3 install \
-    https://repo.radeon.com/rocm/manylinux/rocm-rel-7.2.3/apex-1.9.0%2Brocm7.2.3.git355db9b8-cp312-cp312-linux_x86_64.whl \
-    https://repo.radeon.com/rocm/manylinux/rocm-rel-7.2.3/transformer_engine-2.6.0-py3-none-any.whl \
-    https://repo.radeon.com/rocm/manylinux/rocm-rel-7.2.3/transformer_engine_rocm-2.6.0-py3-none-manylinux_2_28_x86_64.whl
+    https://repo.radeon.com/rocm/manylinux/rocm-rel-7.2.3/apex-1.9.0%2Brocm7.2.3.git355db9b8-cp312-cp312-linux_x86_64.whl
 
-RUN pip install --no-build-isolation  https://repo.radeon.com/rocm/manylinux/rocm-rel-7.2.3/transformer_engine_torch-2.6.0.tar.gz
+# Transformer Engine (ROCm build) 2.18.0.dev0+8c116a51b: the Triton grouped GEMM path that avoids the
+# bf16 grouped-GEMM backward hang on gfx950, and the float-scale blockwise FP8 GEMM kernel.
+ARG TE_WHEEL="transformer_engine-2.18.0.dev0+8c116a51b-cp312-cp312-linux_x86_64.whl"
+ARG TE_WHEEL_URL="https://github.com/PeterYang12/Daily_LLM/releases/download/v0.0.2/${TE_WHEEL}"
+RUN --mount=type=cache,target=/root/.cache/pip \
+    wget -q -O /tmp/${TE_WHEEL} "${TE_WHEEL_URL}" && \
+    pip install --no-build-isolation /tmp/${TE_WHEEL} && \
+    rm /tmp/${TE_WHEEL}
+
+# ROCm 7.2.x driver will not return memory when large torch tensor allocated and 'expandable_segments:True' is on.
+# This issue has been fixed in higher ROCm versions, so a self-built libhsa-runtime bypasses the OOM.
+RUN wget -q https://github.com/PeterYang12/Daily_LLM/releases/download/v0.0.1/libhsa-runtime64.so.1.18.0 && \
+    install -m 0644 /app/libhsa-runtime64.so.1.18.0 /opt/rocm-7.2.3/lib/libhsa-runtime64.so.1.18.70203
 
 RUN --mount=type=cache,target=/root/.cache/pip \
     pip install -U git+https://github.com/ISEEKYAN/mbridge.git@v0.15.1 && \
     pip install mathruler && \
     pip install qwen_vl_utils && \
     pip install flash-linear-attention
 
-ARG MEGATRON_LM_REPO="https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM.git"
-ARG MEGATRON_LM_COMMIT="fd1121b8ff7e3a4f83a28d35aed172d7bc0260e1"
+# NVIDIA/Megatron-LM fd1121b8f plus the DeepSeek-V4 ROCm commits: distributed-optimizer non-leaf fix,
+# config-driven FP8 fake quantization (QAT) and the FP8-training alignment options.
+ARG MEGATRON_LM_REPO="https://github.com/PeterYang12/Megatron-LM.git"
+ARG MEGATRON_LM_BRANCH="deepseek-v4-rocm-support"
 
 COPY docker/rocm/patches /opt/patches
 RUN --mount=type=cache,target=/root/.cache/pip \
     pip install --no-deps "nvidia-modelopt>=0.37.0" "pulp<4.0" && \
-    git clone ${MEGATRON_LM_REPO} /opt/Megatron-LM && \
+    git clone -b ${MEGATRON_LM_BRANCH} ${MEGATRON_LM_REPO} /opt/Megatron-LM && \
     cd /opt/Megatron-LM && \
-    git fetch --depth 1 origin ${MEGATRON_LM_COMMIT} && \
-    git checkout ${MEGATRON_LM_COMMIT} && \
-    git apply /opt/patches/non-leaf-fix.patch && \
     pip install -e . --no-deps
 
-ARG MEGATRON_BRIDGE_REPO="https://github.com/NVIDIA-NeMo/Megatron-Bridge"
-ARG MEGATRON_BRIDGE_COMMIT="v0.5.0"
+# Megatron-Bridge v0.5.0 plus the ue8m0 export fix: the FP8 weight export keeps the power-of-two
+# scale grid of the DeepSeek-V4 checkpoint instead of re-rounding every weight on each sync.
+ARG MEGATRON_BRIDGE_REPO="https://github.com/PeterYang12/Megatron-Bridge"
+ARG MEGATRON_BRIDGE_BRANCH="deepseek-v4-rocm-support"
 
 RUN pip install --no-deps --no-build-isolation --ignore-requires-python \
-    git+${MEGATRON_BRIDGE_REPO}@${MEGATRON_BRIDGE_COMMIT}
+    git+${MEGATRON_BRIDGE_REPO}@${MEGATRON_BRIDGE_BRANCH}
 
 RUN pip install "transformers==5.12.1"  "TransferQueue==0.1.10"
 
-ARG BUILD_DATE="2026-08-07"
+# vLLM 0.26.0 fixes needed by DeepSeek-V4 on ROCm (see the header of each patch for the upstream change):
+#   sparse-topk-guard  NaN logits from the FP8 indexer cache break the radix top-k
+#   cumem-wake         release cached allocator memory before CuMem wake (vllm#49857)
+#   indexer-blockflat  indexer K-cache layout on gfx950/gfx942 (vllm#50455)
+#   swiglu-clamp       FP8 Triton fused MoE dropped the SwiGLU clamp
+RUN cd /usr/local/lib/python3.12/dist-packages && \
+    patch -p1 < /opt/patches/vllm-dsv4-rocm-sparse-topk-guard.patch && \
+    patch -p1 < /opt/patches/vllm-cumem-wake-empty-cache.patch && \
+    patch -p1 < /opt/patches/vllm-dsv4-indexer-blockflat-layout.patch && \
+    patch -p1 < /opt/patches/vllm-dsv4-triton-moe-swiglu-clamp.patch && \
+    cd /app
+
+ARG BUILD_DATE="2026-10-08"
+ARG VERL_REPO="https://github.com/PeterYang12/verl.git"
+ARG VERL_BRANCH="dsv4-rocm"
 RUN --mount=type=cache,target=/root/.cache/pip \
-    git clone https://github.com/verl-project/verl.git && \
+    git clone -b ${VERL_BRANCH} ${VERL_REPO} && \
     cd verl && \
     pip install -e .
 
 ENV VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1
 ENV VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE=1
 
 WORKDIR /app/verl
-CMD ["/bin/bash"]
\ No newline at end of file
+CMD ["/bin/bash"]

@@ -0,0 +1,22 @@
+Backport of vllm-project/vllm#49857 onto vLLM 0.26.0.
+
+Release transient Python and accelerator allocator memory before CuMem wake
+remaps sleeping allocations. During an RL weight refit the rollout worker
+builds temporary device tensors (dtype conversion, MXFP4/FP8 requantization,
+kernel-layout swizzling). They are freed but stay in PyTorch's caching
+allocator as reserved-not-allocated, which create_and_map() cannot use, so
+wake_up(["kv_cache"]) can OOM even though the allocator reports free capacity.
+
+diff --git a/vllm/device_allocator/cumem.py b/vllm/device_allocator/cumem.py
+--- a/vllm/device_allocator/cumem.py
++++ b/vllm/device_allocator/cumem.py
+@@ -291,6 +291,9 @@ class CuMemAllocator:
+                 back to GPU memory. If None, all memory allocation will be loaded
+                 back to GPU memory.
+         """
++        gc.collect()
++        torch.accelerator.empty_cache()
++
+         for ptr, data in self.pointer_to_data.items():
+             if tags is None or data.tag in tags:
+                 handle = data.handle

@@ -0,0 +1,285 @@
+# Port of vllm-project/vllm#50455 (not yet merged as of 2026-09-08).
+#
+# The DSv4 compressor writes the sparse-indexer K cache block-flat, but every
+# reader takes the tile-shuffled branch when block_size > 1: AITER's
+# deepgemm_fp8_paged_mqa_logits via Preshuffle=True on decode, and
+# cp_gather_indexer_k_quant_cache_triton on prefill. So the indexer scores
+# queries against permuted keys.
+#
+# Verified on this stack (gfx950 / MI350, aiter 0.1.16.post3, block_size=64):
+# AITER's output matches a tile-shuffled reading of the cache at cos=1.000000,
+# and against the correct block-flat reading its top-512 selection overlaps by
+# only 58% at 2K context and 26% at 8K (top-8 overlap 3% and 0%).
+#
+# This routes decode/MTP through a Triton kernel that reads the true layout and
+# switches the prefill gather to NORMAL. The replacement kernel matches a
+# block-flat torch reference to ~2e-5 relative with an identical top-512 on
+# gfx950, for decode and MTP, at block_size 64 and 256. It also casts the page
+# id to int64, which additionally avoids the 32-bit block-offset overflow
+# reported in vllm-project/vllm#52109.
+#
+# End-to-end on DeepSeek-V4-Flash-Base-7L, GRPO, 2 samples per arm:
+#
+#   8192-token responses      stock            with fix
+#   rollout_corr/kl           0.0132  0.0137   0.0088  0.0072
+#   rollout_probs_diff_mean   0.0166  0.0169   0.0138  0.0119
+#   rollout_probs_diff_max    0.750   0.578    0.427   0.395
+#   pearson                   0.9963  0.9963   0.9975  0.9980
+#
+# Length matters because the indexer scores tokens/compress_ratio candidates and
+# compress_ratio is 4 on the DSA layers, so index_topk=512 discards nothing until
+# a sequence passes ~2048 tokens. At 2048-token responses (~551 candidates, 7%
+# discarded) the fix is inside run-to-run noise; at 8192 (~2087 candidates, 75%
+# discarded) it cuts the train/rollout KL by ~40%.
+#
+# Apply after vllm-dsv4-rocm-sparse-topk-guard.patch: that patch's decode-side
+# nan_to_num_ guard stays on the AITER path, which DSv32/GLM still use.
+--- a/vllm/v1/attention/ops/rocm_aiter_mla_sparse.py	2026-09-08 16:04:29.351098722 +0000
++++ b/vllm/v1/attention/ops/rocm_aiter_mla_sparse.py	2026-09-08 16:04:29.351098722 +0000
+@@ -223,6 +223,7 @@
+     token_to_seq: torch.Tensor,

++    # scale_region_off = block_size*D//4 needs D % 4 == 0 (D=128).

++    row = tl.program_id(0)
++    split = tl.program_id(1)

++    n = row % NEXT_N
++    if CTX_PER_ROW:
++        seq_len = tl.load(ctx_lens_ptr + row)

++        seq_len = tl.load(ctx_lens_ptr + b) - NEXT_N + n + 1

++    h = tl.arange(0, NUM_HEADS)

inline_comments.body:
Answering my own question after checking: **yes, this patch also applies on CUDA**, and I'd prefer not to land it in its current form.

- `apply_patch()` runs for every `MLATransformerConfig` model (`hf_to_mcore_config_dpskv3` and `make_megatron_module`), regardless of platform. The new function only checks whether `csa` can be imported, and any recent mcore has that module.
- CUDA reaches the unfused path too. In `fd1121b8f`, `apply_dsa_kernel_fusion` defaults to `False`. In upstream `main`, `use_fused_dsa_kernels(config)` falls back to unfused when the backend is unfused or when FlashMLA / cuDNN CuTe-DSL is missing. All call sites in `csa.py` resolve the name from the module globals, so the replacement is used everywhere.

More importantly, **upstream has already fixed this**. NVIDIA/Megatron-LM#6400 (`a2003d48f`, merged 2026-08-27) changed `unfused_compressed_sparse_attn` to `kv_flat.index_select(0, ...)` with the same rationale. Your fork's base `fd1121b8f` (2026-07-10) predates it. With an mcore that already has the fix, this patch:
- overwrites the upstream implementation with a frozen copy and drops upstream's `attn_sink` shape validation;
- will break (`TypeError`) or silently diverge if upstream later changes the signature or the index semantics (e.g. THD);
- is applied silently, with no log line, so it would be hard to spot during debugging.

Suggestions:
1. Preferred: cherry-pick #6400 into the `deepseek-v4-rocm-support` fork (or rebase onto a newer mcore), point the Dockerfile at it, and drop this verl patch.
2. If it has to stay for now, gate it on the old implementation rather than on the platform, e.g. only patch when `"torch.gather" in inspect.getsource(csa.unfused_compressed_sparse_attn)`, and log when the patch is applied. CUDA users on an old mcore with fusion off would hit the same OOM, so an `is_rocm` check alone isn't the right gate.

The Dockerfile, vLLM patches and recipe are ROCm-only and don't affect CUDA.
